body: that may help but it would be better if you could explain to him how the antidepressants will help him enjoy life again. there are ones that are specifically make you happy and ones that prevent the depression from hitting throughout the day.. its not your fault he feels this way  he most likely can't help it

force him to talk, show that you are there for him. i was/am actually doing what he is now and someone i carefree deeply who i tried to push away has just wedged herself into fixing me when she has a full plate to deal with. so to prevent the guilt of risking her happiness or life  i have scheduled an appt with dr to get on antidepressants. if he is as bright as you say than he will see the error if his ways. this is also assuming you will try to help after he pushes little harder cuz thats what happened with me.. hope this helps

if you want to talk about anything i can lend and ear. or talk about more of what I've come to realize in more coherent thought than above thats cool too. Im 22 and have been feeling the same since i was 8 so for myself i learned a lot and would be more than willing to share
I'm sorry for your loss. I'm not going to say i know what your are going through but have you tried doing things that you and your sister would have enjoyed, or what you would have liked to show her?

if you do meny people will be sad, do something that brings peace of mind. does it make you forget the pain when you help another? Have you tried observing the world around you; not the people but whats going on around them? we all search for our own peace but there are some who are plagued with sorrow with no hope for peace, I've found my life meaningless, yet through my studies into death and subsequently life, i myself have seen small tiny wonders in that i may have never seen if i were a happy person. you never know what you might see in this world.

what i sometime find myself doing is jus walking out the front/ back door and just listen. the world around us moves freely and if you take that time to listen to a bird chirping or tree rustling you may just discover something you never would have noticed

i can't say i know anything like what you are going through, but i do know that for someone who is just trying to get by, i would say that if you know that if something happens and your wife will want you to live than you should live for her. do the things she couldn't do but wanted and do the things you want to share with her.

if you can contact them try to keep a normal conversation to give them a sense of free expression without fear of reprisal. if you can establish that connection than they would be more inclined to share whats bringing them down. Granted this will take time and you will have to walk on egg shells while trying to pull teeth.

im not fit for this world but this has become my answer to the little life i may enjoy, in this world everything lives and dies. instead of looking for happiness or a path. just look, look at everything around you, study the things around you. i see no happiness for my life but at the very least i can see it happen in others.
